html:
Kenesary Kasymov was a Kazakh sultan, grandson of Ablai Khan, who led a revolt against Russian rule from 1837 to 1847. He was born in 1802 and is remembered as the last khan of the Kazakhs.

Russia had abolished the Kazakh khans in the 1820s and was building forts deep in the steppe. Kenesary raised an army, attacked the forts, was proclaimed khan in 1841 and set up a small state with its own taxes. Russian columns and Kazakh rivals pushed him south.

In 1847 he crossed into the lands of the Kyrgyz, where he was defeated and killed. His head was sent to the Russian governor. The rising failed, and the Russian Empire went on to take the whole steppe. In independent Kazakhstan he is a national hero, with a statue in Astana, though in Kyrgyzstan he is remembered as an invader of the Kyrgyz.
